Honestly after a few games and trying only a few of the many weapons out. I have now unlocked the amazing ability to understand why Indiana Jones dreaded snakes. I successfully managed to gain Ophidiophobia (take a guess at what that fear is about) after someone acquired the the [b]Snake Rocket Launcher[/b]. yet somehow i manage to always find myself only with a pistol.
Now this game really stands out if you have friends to play it with. [i]Honestly even with randoms it's still a blast either way.[/i]
[h1]Pros: [/h1]
-The game is fairly cheap. During sales, the cost is [b] much[/b] lower. (Shocking I know)
-Can be very entertaining due to it's RNG-like gameplay
-The game is very simple to learn.
-The weapons are very unique. Often ranging from regular pistols, to snake grenade launchers.
-Gave me ophidiophobia
-The maps can be very bizarre and at other times very simple
-The cartoon feeling fits well with the gameplay
-Can support up to 4 players per game
-Split-screen works well
-[u]Snakes.[/u]
-The moments where you say something like, "I GOT BESTED BY A CRIPPLED GUY WITH A JAVELIN"
-The games are often very quick, and you don't need to wait too long.
-You catch on the key mechanics of the game, within 15 minutes
-Any weapon that involve snakes.

[h1]Neutral: [/h1]
-"Is that a Snake I shot out of this minigun?"
-"Oh I can shoot them out forever!"
-"WAIT WHY ARE THEY ATTACKING ME"
-"BAD SNAKES, I AM YOUR  LORD"
-[i]Enemy blue player, shoots snake rocket launcher[/i]
-I have never screamed more in my entire life.

[h1]Cons: [/h1]
Every game has some flaws and this is no exception.
-Bugs are sometimes frequent, but they don't cause too many issues.
-There is no training mode.
-The map making system needs more stuff.
-The player who gets a weapon first, will often be the winner. So the winner comes down to that practically
-Repetitive
-It's quite fun indeed. But you'll need friends for it to last

Overall this is a great game, that I have honestly haven't been able to play much. I would rate it an 8/10.

Let me get one thing straight, I am not giving this game a bad review because it is a bad game. For couch play or just playing online with your friends? Really fun. Online with random people can still be really fun. But something I run into really often is hackers. It happens really often and is annoying. So if you are buying the game to play with friends, get it because it is just a blast with friends. But if you are just getting it to play online with people you don't know, just take caution. And, for the love of GOD please don't be a hacker. It takes the fun away.

I finally did it. I out pizza'd the Hut. It was the greatest mistake of my life.

After years of perfecting my recipe, I made my way down to the local hut, fresh-baked pizza pie in hand. "Try this," I told the kid working the counter. He did, and he had to agree that it was better than anything Pizza Hut had to offer. Soon, the entire store, customers included, was feasting on my delicious pie. The manager walked over, grabbed a slice, and took a bite. I look at him, anticipation rising. This was the boss, the local fief lord of the Hut. His approval meant more to me than all the rest combined. He took a bite and nodded. "I'll be damned," he said, "you really did it. You out- pizza'd the Hut. Shame." Shame? What did he mean by tha-- the manager pulled a gun out from behind his apron and shot the nearest customer in the head. "We have a Code Jalapeño," he said into his wrist as he executed the remaining customers. "I repeat, we have a Code Jalapeño." The ground was slick with blood. The kid working the counter choked out his dying breath as the manager turned to me. "You just had to do it motherfucker. You just had to out pizza the Hut." He shoved the gun in my face. I was too scared to fight, too scared to run. The manager pulled the trigger.

A click. The gun was empty. I threw a chair at the manager and scrambled out of the Pizza Hut, not even bothering to see if my missile hit its mark. I was closely pursued by the manager, who had gotten his hands on a deadly sharp pizza cutter. I suspected in his hands it would cut more than pizza. Somehow, I was able to get into my car and speed off, the manager cursing my existence as I left him behind. I took a deep breath. The manager was clearly psychotic. Yes, that was it, just a crazy man with a gun. It had to be. My phone rang. Sister. I picked it. "They're dead, she sobbed. They're all dead. Mom, Dad, Chris, Bill. Dead. They killed them all." I could barely understand her, so great were her sobs. "What do you mean? Where are you?" I asked urgently. "How is this possi--" A single gunshot sounded through my phone's speakers. Silence. Then, I heard a man's voice. "No one out pizzas the Hut." He hung up. I drove down the empty country road, mind blank. I had nothing. They killed my family. I was alone.

At that moment I knew what I had to do. They took everything from me. Well then, I would take everything from them. Pizza Hut was so terrified of being out pizza'd, they forgot there's one thing worse than a man with a recipe: A man with nothing to lose. I'll give them a limited time offer they won't be able to refuse: two bullets for the price of one.

With a free side order of pain.

Well, I found this game kind of randomly. I think I saw the trailer for it because I had the april fools day Totally Accurate Battle Zombilator or something like that. And, I'm gonna rate it just like all of my other reviews! 1 to 10 scale!

Graphics: 9/10: The graphics in this game are crisp and smooth. Though, explosions aren't quite optimized, and i'd love to see some sort of extra distinguishing marks like maybe hats or something similar added later. And certainly a Colorblind Mode for those gamers who can't see certain colors!

Audio: 10/10: The Music and Sounds for this game are a mix of funky techno and awesome gunshot noises. Though I'd have loved to hear an AWP noise from CS:GO for the Sniper Rifle.

Gameplay: 9.5/10: I will certainly get hundreds of hours out of this with friends. The gameplay is like an older PS3 game a friend had where you could Twin Stick and you had a Punch, Kick, and Energy button setup. And there were random weapons that would spawn. I would like the ability to go into a Training Room with each of the weapons to learn how they play, and some sort of Health Meter would be nice, but not required. 

Maps: 9/10: The maps are great and fun to play, But i'd love to see some sort of Map Creator linked to the Steam Workshop Mods system. This would help to keep the game alive unlike other similar and still fun Indie titles like Screencheat, where the game is great, but the small map pool killed the game's potential to purely a few hours and then moving on with my life. 

Overall: 9/10: People might say that I am being harsh on a brand new Indie title, but these are valid criticisms, and I do only have a few minutes into the game at the time of this review, but I will certainly be racking up the hours as the weeks go by and I need something to put my frustrations into! I highly recommend this game as a fun Party game. Controllers are required and I highly recommend learning how to use the Twin Stick fighting style!

Amazing game that's extremely chaotic but really fun especially with friends. I'd recommend it to anyone who likes multiplayer fighting games but doesn't want to spend too much money because this game is cheap but really fun.

The game is quite unique in terms of tech that can be found in it. 
Blocking and striking at the same time propels you forward at intense speed, you can throw a gun only to pick it back up again to gain an extra jump, parry and much else I just don't remember.

However. The hitboxes are dubious at best. For both the character and weapons. I bet the characters are either server-side or client-side in a way where they often appear displaced.

Can't say the same for weapon hitboxes though. Often when you throw your weapons, if the hitbox so much as graces a pixel, it'll lose it's powerful throwing property but more often than not, the velocity is retained... This has led to, shall I say Unfortunate losses where I've thrown a weapon only for it to be picked up by the enemy...

Man I just want to style on my opponents with the instant kill pistol throw headshot consistently!

Stick Fight: The Game is a simplistic physics-based game that draws its inspiration from stickman fighting animations on the internet. At first sight, it bears a striking resemblance to Gang Beasts in terms of gameplay. In this game too, your sole aim is to beat each other to death and be the last stickman standing and by doing so, you're literally crowned. But ironically, the funniest thing about Stick Fight is dying. Due to the hilarious ways you can die in this game, you will always have a good laugh whenever you die. It's either because of your silly mistake or your opponent's extremely "calculated" shot. 

The levels are designed in a way to challenge the contestants, so that you can use the environment to your advantage if you act cleverly. For instance, in the winter setting, you will have ice which will break when you shoot at and the stickman standing on it will fall to his death. Besides the winter setting, you have for instance, a factory setting with chains holding your platform, a lava setting where the floor is lava and so on. Each level within these settings has a certain pattern that expects you to overcome.

In terms of weapons, except your fists of course, there are pistols, sniper rifles, shotguns, RPG, minigun, laser beams, grenade launchers and last but not least, guns that shoot poisonous snakes. Weapons will also cause a physical reaction due to their exaggerated recoil. So, don't be surprised if you find yourself flying when you're spraying that minigun.  In other words, it's safe to say that the variety of levels and weapons won't let you and your friends get bored fast. 

After the first fun 10 minutes though, you will realize there is no purpose or an end to the game. There is no ultimate winner, no scoreboard or leaderboards whatsoever. So I suggest you don't go into this game expecting more than just having fun and a laugh with your friends. 

As for the controls, I used a controller to play this game since keyboard/mouse felt a bit uncomfortable. It's possible to use multiple controllers too, you can hop into an online game with you two being on the same couch or just play locally. 

If you have friends to play with and you enjoy physics-based games, this title is a must-play. Considering the price tag, the tons of joy you will derive from playing this game for a couple of hours is well worth paying for. Despite the fact that this game is fully released and not in early-access, it continously receives updates, new levels, weapons and features too. So, don't miss out on this one.

[u][h1] Stick Fight: The Game [/h1][/u]
Stick Fight intrigued me. I had been a follower of Landfall's previous games and projects. They had a unique, simplistic art style fitted with a bundle of content. And when I saw this in my email one day at school, I knew I [i]had[/i] to buy it. Me and my friend both loved stick animation since we were as young as 9, and we love party games.
[b]So, what about the game itself?[/b]
[u][h1] Pros ✓ [/h1][/u]
[b][u]The gameplay: [/u][/b]
The gameplay is one of my favourite aspects. Being Landfall, they are bound to have satisfyingly floppy animations, and they deliver. Backflips, frontflips, diving, Naruto running, and so much more is available to do in the world. Me and my friend even RP as different people from different countries thanks to the wide variety of guns and environments. Even though the fighting commences in a closed box, it is the perfect amount of space needed for long range, medium range and melee battling to take place.
[b][u] Graphics [/u][/b]
Not much is to really be said here, one graphics option on a dropdown menu and resolution options. I play at a low resolution, and it's good to know they optimised it well, just like T.A.B.S. It's kind of a shame they didn't allow for particle options, however, as one of the laser levels cuts my framerate to pieces.
[b][u] Servers [/u][/b]
The servers are, for the most part, consistent and steady. However, I would like for there to be more options. I won't babble on too much about this, because the game is only 2 days old, but there is only one mode. Deathmatch. I would like a variety of modes like being able to team up with friends, a gamemode similar to the conveyor belt box level, where you jump and evade boxes or lasers while running. However, the game is only two days old, as I've mentioned. It's subject to development, and they have a huge update coming soon.
[b][u] Developers [/u][/b]
A little side note here, the developers do not have this as their main priority at the moment. It is currently T.A.B.S, and this game is what they have done in their free time. So, if there are no updates for a few months, it's nothing to rally on about. Just be patient and they'll give updates and more content further on.
[b][u] Music [/u][/b]
I really like the music in this game. It fits the tone of messy brawls and speedy jolts, but the music does repeat itself over the course of time, and you will hear the same tune played again after a while. My friend likes to play this game with no music but rather the punching audio, maybe you'll do the same.
[u][h1] Cons ✗ [/h1][/u]
Well, this is going to sound rather preachy, but there are basically no major cons that I can give to the game. Two minor ones I have previously mentioned are the graphics limitations and servers sometimes lagging a tad, but there's basically nothing bad about this game. Maybe the price is something to go against, but a game is a game.
[u][h1] TL:DR [/h1][/u]
This game is utterly fantastic. I recommend buying this game if you need something to play with friends, love fast-paced action or brutal beatdowns. This game does remind me of Gang Beasts, a game I have reviewed negatively in the past, but this is the Gang Beasts everyone wanted. Laughs, beatdowns and difficulty.
This is a great game to have in your library. Over the course of some updates, you might find yourself crawling back to it.

As someone who has, as of the time of this review, played the game for about 162 hours and unlocked every single achievement, I really WANT to say that I love this game. And honestly, sometimes, I do. When the game is working properly, it can be a lot of fun. But unfortunately, the game is filled with all sorts of game-breaking glitches that the developers don't seem to be in any hurry to fix. I took a hiatus from this game for several months out of pure frustration, hoping that when I got back to it, these issues would be resolved, but alas, they have not. During pretty much every play session, I will eventually run into glitches that cause one or more of the following:

1. Player becomes invisible, resulting in me being pummeled by Casper, the Ghost of Kung-Fu as I uselessly flail about in a vain effort to murder the thin air in front of me.
2. Player death does not get recognized by the game, so that even after I've technically won the round, my stick figure stands alone in the ring wondering why he's the only one left standing, only to come to the haunting realization that the only way in which to escape this eternal nightmare is to leap into the unforgiving abyss below, to join his fallen brethren.
3. Player becomes invincible, which is even more annoying than the previous glitch because in addition to the unfairness of not winning a round when you should've, you now have to deal with the aftermath of a realistic Superman vs. Batman fight: one man is left as a bleeding husk on the ground, and the other is left without a scratch. Poor Clark.

I could go on, but these are just the 3 most common glitches that I've noticed. Less commonly, I've also experienced the screen constantly shaking as though the virtual cameraman has suddenly developed aggressive Parkinson's disease; a glitch that caused me to control two stick figures simultaneously, which to be honest was actually sort of fun for a while; and the occasional glitch or two with the black hole gun, causing all sorts of mayhem. I guess it really does warp reality.

If not for all the bugs, this game would be fantastic. Sure, there are balancing issues with some of the weapons, and some of the maps can be frustrating, but these things can be tweaked in the options menu, so I can't really gripe about that. On the whole, the combat system, while simplistic, is fun nonetheless, and there is a lot of room to play around with the game mechanics and physics. However, as it stands, I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone as it is now. Until the developers start focusing more on fixing the game's bugs than they have on their cute little profanity filters, I'm afraid it gets a thumbs-down from me. Which is a real shame because, as I said in the beginning, I truly do want to love this game. I just wish that the developers loved it enough to fix it, too.

Stick Fight: The Game is an overwhelming, tenacious, "flying-around" game that destroys friendships because someone lost their throat from screaming.

You asked for four sticks? Well there you go, this is the game. This game literally exists ladies and gentlemen, as I have no clue why a madman would want to create this so called masterpiece that everyone keeps talking about. Five dollars is simply something you could waste into just so you can smack someone way across the map like Smash?

Well the gameplay IS SMASH in some ways while the "Gods" from above throw down their trash for us to enjoy and kill each other with. Weapons ranging from your flying kicks and fists to a freaking black hole that consumes the entire game. It's like throwing a warp pipe in the middle of the battlefield, but sucks you in for purposes of making sure you GET TO THE NEXT LEVEL. Level designs differ every stage, offering unique challenges that will literally end each match in seconds, and you will have to blame whoever shoot the barrel first full of explosives, or snakes. Or anyone who shoot the chains that keeps the platform in the stage.

When the gods drops down weapons and everything. It is not just something you can shoot or slash someone with. Once you see a pumpkin falling down, you know one of the four of you are gonna turn tails and try to kill you with the [b]Touhou-style bullet hell[/b] theme. And they aren't kidding when I said it's bullet hell.

Connectivity ranges from being not good to okay I guess, but there will be improvements overtime and that's good. Graphics are simply divine as to how an indie game should be, flawless physics flying around with the amazement done simply by you or your friends alone. Nothing can stop you once you have the black hole, which literally fracks you stuff up. Game balance? What are you talking about? Every fighting has no balance, and this game certainly qualifies as being [i]"Good luck, break a leg."[/i]

Forgot to mention the lobby. You want to know about the lobby? Well if you got friends in the lobby, you can just kill them, and then that starts the match. [i]Game logic at it's best,[/i] but I'm sure thats how an episode in Kitchen Nightmares kicks off.

[b]So what's bad?[/b]

There are gonna be some hiccups that will hinder your experience, and sometimes bugs the heck out of you during the match. When there's so much going on, especially if it involves way too many explosions and physics being executed by every players actions, you will crash. Chances of your game crashing is high enough that it'd be frequent, and sometimes annoying. Although you do have the choice to rejoin back, that is if you are playing with your friends, you'll get another crash that may either be frequent or less. 

I tested the game on both from my business and gaming computers respectively, both suffers from the same crash.

Sometimes when you DO play with your friends, they see something different entirely than what you see in your perspective. You're alive, and they said you aren't. That's some connection that bugs out how really well synced the match is for four people.

You thought I forgot the gameplay issues? Well surprisingly there is little. While there is indeed some fixing needed for the weapons, that's just about it. The gameplay itself isn't generic nor repetitive, because you already lost your keyboard once you stopped playing.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]

[b]I highly recommend that you prepare enough gallons of water[/b] if you're going to play with your friends, have discord/teamspeak on before starting a deathmatch that has no end whatsoever. Because there will be TONS of screaming. TONS. And you won't be able to speak again anymore once you do shout like a madman yourself. If you experience any symptoms while playing this game, seek medical attention immediately [i]( plus some water )[/i]. 

So what is it? Do I recommend this game that you can waste your time fighting sticks to no end? [b]Yes.[/b] Is it worth it's price tag? [b]Depends.[/b]

Did you grow up in the era of Flash animations? I sure did. In particular I recall the ones that centred around stick characters. One really innovative series I remember is a sequence where the stick character fights the animator using all manner of improvised weaponry, as well as another that was a very well choreographed fight scene between a red stick character and like, a hundred others.

So after all this time, I remembered all this from some dusty wrinkle in my brain and wondered "hey, what if there was a game just like this out there and if so, what would it look and play like?"

Cue developers Landfall West (known for Totally Accurate Battle Simulator among others) with their 2017 release of Stick Fight: The Game.

This is a more casual game, so let's start with the gameplay. Stick Fight's premise is simple: be the last one standing in a 1-4 player arena with fast changing maps with their own themes, gimmicks and pitfalls as well as a healthy roster of weapons ranging from pistols, shotguns, assault rifles, sniper rifles, lasers, energy swords and more. There are a couple of seasonal/special mapsets too which have some special conditions like picking up an item to transform, and so on.

Players have a simple but effective set of actions available to them. They can crouch, run, aim (with the right stick or mouse), jump, parkour up walls, clamber (to a degree) and throw melee weapons or guns. Because your action list is quite short, the combat ends up being frenetic, easy to understand and fun without getting too complicated or clunky. This keeps combat feeling fun but fair as well, meaning there aren't things like buffs, perks or stats to get in the way of smashing your opponent.

Graphically, the game is quite pleasing to look at without being too shiny and bloomy. It's a 2D game that doesn't go over the top with fully 3D backgrounds. The artwork is simple and clean with a well defined foreground and background to help keep your eyes on the action. It does have some post-processing effects going on that you can't turn off, but they rarely got in the way with the exception of explosions, which can be quite large and can sometimes block your view for a moment. Fortunately, you can turn down screen shake to your liking in case it's too much for you at 100%.

Each player is assigned their own colour, and while it works I find it can be a little difficult to track your player when things get really intense, in particular with the blue and green player colours. One thing that could help with this is to give each player a few coloured presets to choose from, in case the default colour isn't bright or clear enough for them.

Paired with the graphics is some beefy sound. The intro theme music is really catchy and bassy, without being too intense to wear you down over time. Player sounds are pretty sparse, there are no callouts from characters and the only sounds you hear are footsteps and weapon impacts. This leaves most of the soundscape up to the music and the gunplay.

The guns, for the most part, sound meaty and are fun to fire, with the exception of one or two guns that are fine, but sound a bit weak like the needlegun. So overall, the sound is pretty well done, with bonus points for being meaty in general.

So, let's cut to the chase, the game is fun right? So, we get the game, we install it, we hop into quick play and... there's no one else to play with. Yeah, it's a bit devoid of players at the moment. I'm not exactly sure why this is the case, perhaps the game just hasn't been updated that much on Steam or maybe the playerbase wanted a few more maps and weapons, and have since moved on to something else. Maybe no one even knows about this game. Either way, you're not completely out of luck.

You have the option to play the entire game in couch coop, so it's a great excuse to get a few friends around, order a pizza and catch up while you duke it out. Alternatively, you can just invite your friends through Steam for an online match. The developers have stated publicly that they don't have any plans to update the game right now, so I don't think we will see bots in the future. As a game to play with your friends though, it hits the mark pretty nicely.

There's also the ability to download content through the Workshop on Steam, so make sure to take advantage of that once you've had your fill of the vanilla maps.

If someone asked me whether this game was worth $7.50AUD, as long as they had a friend to play with I would agree. I'm not sure if the game goes on sale but if it does, maybe consider grabbing the party pack to share with your online friends. If it gets any future updates, even better.
